BranchManagementOutcome.title: Phase outcome
BranchManagementOutcome.description: `nothing-to-release` — no changesets were found, so no branch or PR work was needed. A SUCCESS: nothing failed. `branch-created` — the release branch and its PR were created. `branch-updated` — an existing release branch and PR were brought up to date. `branch-unchanged` — the release branch already matched the plan and needed no push. `conflicted` — the release branch could not be updated because the merge conflicted; the only failing outcome for this phase.

BranchManagementFailureStage.title: Failure stage
BranchManagementFailureStage.description: WHEN the phase failed. `plan` — the release plan could not be read; `branch` — the release branch could not be created or updated (a merge conflict is the usual cause); `pull-request` — the release PR could not be opened or updated.

reason.title: Failure reason
reason.description: WHAT went wrong, as a single-line summary.

changesetFiles.title: Changeset files
changesetFiles.description: Changeset files observed in `.changeset/`. NOT the workspace count — one file may name several workspaces, and two files may name the same one, so the two diverge in both directions.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.description: Workspaces the release plan versions. Includes those pulled in only because a dependency moved, which name no changeset of their own.

BranchManagementTotals.title: Totals
BranchManagementTotals.description: Aggregate counts, so a consumer does not have to reduce the changeset list.

name.title: Release branch name
name.description: The git branch name the release PR targets and changeset versioning lands on.

existed.title: Branch existed
existed.description: True when the release branch already existed before this run; false when it was just created.

created.title: Branch created
created.description: True when this run created the release branch.

updated.title: Branch updated
updated.description: True when this run pushed new commits to the release branch (changeset version bumps, etc.).

hasConflicts.title: Has conflicts
hasConflicts.description: True when the release branch could not be cleanly fast-forwarded over the target branch and a merge conflict was detected. When true, the release branch needs manual conflict resolution before subsequent runs can complete; the action will keep failing on this branch until the conflict is resolved.

BranchManagementReleaseBranch.title: Release branch state
BranchManagementReleaseBranch.description: The state of the release branch after Phase 1 — whether it existed, was created/updated, and any conflicts.

number.title: Release PR number
number.description: The GitHub PR number for the release PR.

url.title: Release PR URL
url.description: The HTML URL of the release PR on GitHub.

action.title: Release PR action
action.description: Whether this run created the release PR or updated an existing one.

BranchManagementReleasePr.title: Release PR state
BranchManagementReleasePr.description: The release PR's number, URL, and the action this run took on it. Null when no PR was created (no changesets to release).

ChangesetsBumpType.title: Changeset bump type
ChangesetsBumpType.description: The bump the release plan applies to this package: `major`, `minor`, or `patch`. The validation phase emits an extended set under `ValidationBumpType` that adds `new` and `unknown`.

name.title: Package name
name.description: The npm package name this release covers.

changesetCount.title: Changesets naming this package
changesetCount.description: How many changeset files name this package. **Zero means the package releases only because a dependency did** — it still gets a version bump and a CHANGELOG entry, but no changeset asked for it, so it is invisible to a count of changeset files. Renders as the `—` in a release table's changeset column.

oldVersion.title: Current version
oldVersion.description: The package's version before this release, as recorded in its `package.json` on the target branch.

newVersion.title: Next version
newVersion.description: The version this release will publish, after applying `bumpType`. Known in Phase 1 because it comes from the release plan rather than from the changeset files.

BranchManagementChangesetPackage.title: Changeset package
BranchManagementChangesetPackage.description: One package the release plan covers, with its bump and whether a changeset asked for it.

count.title: Changeset count
count.description: The number of changeset **files** observed in the `.changeset/` directory. Not the length of `packages`: one file may name several packages, and two files may name the same one, so the two numbers diverge in both directions.

packages.title: Changeset packages
packages.description: Every package this release will version, from the release plan — including packages bumped only because a dependency moved, which `changesetCount: 0` identifies. Empty array when there is nothing to release; the phase reports `outcome: "nothing-to-release"` in that case, which is a success — nothing failed.

BranchManagementChangesets.title: Changesets observed
BranchManagementChangesets.description: What this run will release — the number of changeset files, and every package the release plan versions with its bump and whether a changeset named it explicitly.

BranchManagementPayload.title: Branch Management payload
BranchManagementPayload.description: Phase 1 outcome — the release-branch ensure/create result, the release PR (created or updated, null when no changesets), and the changesets observed in `.changeset/` with their derived per-package bumps.

$schema.title: JSON Schema URL
$schema.description: URL of the hosted JSON Schema this output conforms to. Editors and json-schema-aware consumers use this for hover docs and validation.

phase.title: Phase discriminator
phase.description: `branch-management` identifies this as a Phase 1 output.

success.title: Succeeded
success.description: The one boolean a consumer should gate on. True when the phase completed with nothing failed — including a run that had nothing to do, which is a success because nothing failed. Read `outcome` for what specifically happened.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One human-readable sentence describing the run. Derived from the structured fields beside it and never authored independently, so the prose cannot drift from the data.

dryRun.title: Dry run
dryRun.description: True when the action ran with `dry-run: true`. Phase 3 publishes nothing in dry-run mode; Phases 1 and 2 still observe and report, but mutations (branch updates, PR creation/updating) are suppressed.

failure.title: Failure
failure.description: Why and where the phase failed. Null when `success` is true.

BranchManagementOutput.title: Branch Management output (Phase 1)
BranchManagementOutput.description: The structured `result` output emitted when the action runs in the branch-management phase (Phase 1). Triggered by a push to the target branch; ensures/creates the release branch and the release PR.

examples.summary: 1 changeset file · 1 workspace to version · release PR created

ValidationOutcome.title: Phase outcome
ValidationOutcome.description: `validated` — every build passed and no check raised an error finding. `nothing-to-release` — no workspace had a version difference against the target branch, so there was nothing to validate; a SUCCESS, because nothing failed. It usually means the release already merged, or Phase 1 did not commit the expected bumps, and a warning-severity finding is emitted alongside it. `build-failed` — a build failed, so the publish dry-runs never ran and their check rows report the cascade rather than a result of their own. `checks-failed` — builds passed but at least one check produced an error finding.

ValidationFailureStage.title: Failure stage
ValidationFailureStage.description: WHEN validation failed. `build` — a workspace build failed, which cascades to every downstream check; `publish-validation` — a publish dry-run failed or could not be completed; `sbom` — SBOM generation or its NTIA check failed; `release-notes` — the release-notes preview could not be produced.

reason.title: Failure reason
reason.description: WHAT went wrong, as a single-line summary.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.description: Workspaces with a version difference against the target branch.

githubOnly.title: GitHub-only workspaces
githubOnly.description: Workspaces that resolved no publish target — versioned, tagged and released, publishing to no registry. Zero builds is their steady state, not a failure.

githubWithPackages.title: Registry-publishing workspaces
githubWithPackages.description: Workspaces that resolved at least one publish target.

checksWarning.title: Checks with warnings
checksWarning.description: Validation checks whose status is `warning` — neither passed nor failed. Carried so the three counts sum to the number of checks; folding warnings into either bucket loses them.

errorFindings.title: Error findings
errorFindings.description: Findings of `error` severity. Any of these makes `success` false.

warningFindings.title: Warning findings
warningFindings.description: Findings of `warning` severity. These do NOT make `success` false unless the run set `strict-warnings`.

ValidationTotals.title: Totals
ValidationTotals.description: Aggregate counts, so a consumer does not have to reduce the package, check and finding arrays.

passed.title: Build validation passed
passed.description: True when every released package built successfully.

packageCount.title: Package count
packageCount.description: Number of packages built and validated.

ValidationBuildValidation.title: Build validation summary
ValidationBuildValidation.description: Summary of the build-validation step: whether every package built, and how many were built.

name.title: Check name
name.description: Row label for the Validation Checks table. Canonical five-row set today: 'Build Validation', 'Link Issues', 'Publish Validation', 'Release Notes Preview', 'SBOM Preview'.

status.title: Check status
status.description: `pass` — the check passed; `warning` — the check raised a non-blocking warning; `error` — the check failed and blocks the release.

outcome.title: Outcome message
outcome.description: Short human-readable summary of the check's outcome (e.g. counts, registry names, error class).

anyOf.title: Check URL
anyOf.description: URL pointing to detail for this check (a check-run URL or external report). Null when no URL applies.

ValidationCheck.title: Validation check row
ValidationCheck.description: One row of the five-row Validation Checks table shown in the release PR comment and the unified check-run summary.

anyOf.title: Package name
anyOf.description: The npm package name the finding concerns. When non-null, equals the `name` of an entry in `publish.packages[]`. When null, the finding is global to the validation run rather than tied to a specific package.

anyOf.title: Build directory
anyOf.description: The build output directory the finding concerns, package-relative. When non-null, equals the `directory` of an entry in the owning package's `builds[]`. When null, the finding concerns the package as a whole rather than a specific build.

ValidationFindingScope.title: Validation finding scope
ValidationFindingScope.description: What a non-pass finding concerns: which package and which of its build directories. `package` is null for global findings; `directory` is null for findings not tied to a specific build directory.

severity.title: Finding severity
severity.description: `error` — fails the validation phase; the release PR is blocked from merging until resolved. `warning` — advisory only and does not block the release; the comment surfaces it for the author to read.

check.title: Owning check
check.description: The validation check that produced this finding (e.g. `Build Validation`, `Publish Validation`). Equal to the `name` of an entry in `checks[]`. Consumers can group findings under their owning check by joining on this value.

message.title: Finding message
message.description: Human-readable description of the finding, suitable for direct display in the release PR comment.

ValidationFinding.title: Validation finding
ValidationFinding.description: Every non-pass validation outcome — `error` fails the check and blocks the release; `warning` is advisory. Findings are projected for the release PR comment and for downstream consumers of the `result` output.

ValidationBumpType.title: Bump type
ValidationBumpType.description: The validation phase's package bump type, derived by diffing the release-branch version against the target-branch version. A superset of `ChangesetsBumpType` (Phase 1 declared bumps): `major`/`minor`/`patch` when the `major.minor.patch` core advanced (entering pre mode, `3.0.4` → `3.0.5-beta.0`, is a `patch`); `graduation` for a prerelease leaving pre mode for its own stable version (`3.0.5-beta.0` → `3.0.5`); `prerelease` for a step inside pre mode on the same core (`-beta.0` → `-beta.1`); `new` when no prior published version exists on the target branch; `unknown` when a version does not parse or the version did not advance.

ValidationWorkspaceOutcome.title: Workspace outcome
ValidationWorkspaceOutcome.description: `validated` — every publication passed its dry-run probe. `nothing-to-validate` — a `github-only` workspace, or one whose every registry target excludes this version through its `releases` channel: it publishes nowhere, so there is nothing to probe, and this is the complete, correct outcome rather than an absence of one. `skipped` — every publication was intentionally not probed. `partial` — some passed and at least one failed. `failed` — probes ran and none passed. Mirrors the publish phase's workspace `outcome` field; the VALUES differ because a dry-run probe and an upload have different results.

ValidationWorkspaceKind.title: Workspace kind
ValidationWorkspaceKind.description: The same vocabulary the publish phase reports, so one word means one thing across the whole run. `github-only` — the workspace resolved no publish target; its release is a version bump, a git tag and a GitHub release. This is the steady state for a private tracking package, not a degraded `github-with-packages`. `github-with-packages` — it resolved at least one publish target (including one the `releases` filter drops for this version). Replaces the old `versionOnly` boolean, which named the same fact in a vocabulary the publish phase did not share.

name.title: Registry display name
name.description: Human-readable registry name, e.g. `npm`, `GitHub Packages`, or the host of a custom registry.

type.title: Registry type
type.description: `npm` — the public npm registry; `github-packages` — GitHub Packages; `jsr` — the JSR registry; `custom` — any other registry configured through the `custom-registries` input. A custom registry usually speaks the npm protocol, but is reported as `custom` rather than `npm` so it is never mistaken for the public registry.

url.title: Registry URL
url.description: The registry endpoint this package was published to.

PublishRegistry.title: Registry
PublishRegistry.description: The registry a package was published to, classified and named.

ValidationPackageOutcome.title: Outcome
ValidationPackageOutcome.description: `ready` — the dry-run publish probe succeeded; `skipped` — the target was intentionally not probed (unconfigured, or filtered out); `failed` — the probe failed and this publication would not land; see `error`. The VALUES differ from the publish phase's (`published`/`recovered`/`failed`/`blocked`) because a probe and an upload have different outcomes — but the field pair is the same, so `success` gates both.

componentCount.title: Component count
componentCount.description: Number of components (direct + transitive dependencies) in the BOM. 0 is legitimate for a dependency-free package.

ntiaCompliant.title: NTIA compliant
ntiaCompliant.description: True when the BOM satisfies every NTIA minimum-elements field. False when at least one field is missing — see `missingNtiaFields`.

missingNtiaFields.title: Missing NTIA fields
missingNtiaFields.description: Names of the NTIA minimum-elements fields the BOM is missing. Empty when `ntiaCompliant` is true.

ValidationBuildSbom.title: SBOM preview
ValidationBuildSbom.description: Per-build SBOM preview: component count, NTIA minimum-elements compliance, and the list of missing NTIA fields when not compliant.

name.title: Published package name
name.description: The package name as it would be published. NOT necessarily the workspace's own name — a workspace may publish under a different name per target.

version.title: Version
version.description: The version this publication would carry.

success.title: Succeeded
success.description: The boolean gate, true only for `outcome: ready`. Named to match the publish phase's package entry, so one filter works across both.

anyOf.title: Error message
anyOf.description: Why the dry-run failed. Non-null only when `outcome` is `failed`.

access.title: Access level
access.description: `public` — would publish publicly; `restricted` — would publish privately (scoped, restricted access).

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: True when this target supports and would emit npm OIDC sigstore provenance attestations.

directory.title: Build directory
directory.description: Package-relative path to the output directory this publication packs from. Packages sharing a directory share one tarball, packed once.

anyOf.title: Packed size (bytes)
anyOf.description: Size of the packed tarball. Null when the dry-run did not report it.

anyOf.title: Unpacked size (bytes)
anyOf.description: Size of the unpacked contents. Null when the dry-run did not report it.

anyOf.title: File count
anyOf.description: Files in the packed tarball. Null when the dry-run did not report it.

sbom.title: SBOM preview
sbom.description: The SBOM that would be generated for this build. Null when generation failed or none applies.

ValidationPackage.title: Package to publish
ValidationPackage.description: One package a workspace would publish to one registry, mirroring the publish phase's per-package entry so the two phases describe the same publications the same way.

status.title: Found
status.description: The CHANGELOG.md was found and the section for the new version was successfully extracted.

content.title: Release notes content
content.description: The extracted Markdown content of the CHANGELOG.md section for the new version.

ReleaseNotesFound.title: Release notes found
ReleaseNotesFound.description: The CHANGELOG.md exists and the section for the new version was located and extracted.

status.title: No CHANGELOG.md
status.description: The package has no CHANGELOG.md file — no release notes can be extracted.

ReleaseNotesNoChangelog.title: Release notes — no CHANGELOG.md
ReleaseNotesNoChangelog.description: The package has no CHANGELOG.md file. This is non-fatal; the GitHub release is created with the version-bump summary instead.

status.title: Version not found
status.description: The CHANGELOG.md exists but no section for the new version was found.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Human-readable explanation of why the version section was not located (e.g. parser couldn't find a matching heading).

ReleaseNotesVersionNotFound.title: Release notes — version not found
ReleaseNotesVersionNotFound.description: The CHANGELOG.md exists but no section for the new version was found.

status.title: Error
status.description: An error occurred while attempting to read or parse the CHANGELOG.md.

message.title: Error message
message.description: The error message from the failed read/parse operation.

ReleaseNotesError.title: Release notes — error
ReleaseNotesError.description: An error occurred while attempting to read or parse the CHANGELOG.md. Non-fatal — the release still proceeds; the GitHub Release body falls back to an auto-generated bump summary.

ValidationReleaseNotes.title: Release notes extraction
ValidationReleaseNotes.description: Discriminated outcome of reading the package's CHANGELOG.md (already populated by `changeset version`) and locating the section for the new version: `found`, `no-changelog`, `version-not-found`, or `error`.

version.title: New version
version.description: The new semver version this release would publish.

anyOf.title: Base version
anyOf.description: The previously published version this release is bumped from. Null when this is the first publish.

anyOf.title: Changeset count
anyOf.description: Number of changesets contributing to this package's bump. Null when unknown.

success.title: Succeeded
success.description: True when every publication this workspace would make passed its dry-run probe. True by construction for a `github-only` workspace, which makes none. Named to match the publish phase's workspace entry.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One human-readable sentence describing this workspace's validation. Derived from the fields beside it and never authored independently, so it cannot drift from them — the same contract the publish phase's workspace `summary` carries.
examples: No registry target — nothing to validate; releases on GitHub only.

packages.title: Packages to publish
packages.description: One entry per (package, registry) publication this workspace would make — the same unit and shape the publish phase reports, so the two can be compared directly. **Always an empty array for a `github-only` workspace**, and never null. Replaces the `builds[].targets[]` nesting, which every consumer had to flatten before it could line up with what publish reported.

ValidationWorkspace.title: Released workspace
ValidationWorkspace.description: A workspace being released this run, with its bump type, kind, builds, per-target readiness, and the extracted release notes. Keyed by workspace name in `validation.workspaces`, so the name is the key rather than a field.

url.title: Check-run URL
url.description: The HTML URL of the unified Release Validation Summary check-run.

conclusion.title: Check-run conclusion
conclusion.description: The GitHub check-run conclusion enum: `success`, `failure`, `neutral`, `cancelled`, `skipped`, `timed_out`, or `action_required`.

ValidationCheckRun.title: Validation check-run
ValidationCheckRun.description: The unified Release Validation Summary check-run produced by the validation phase. Null when no check-run was created.

checks.title: Validation checks
checks.description: The five-row Validation Checks table — one entry per validation step run this phase. Canonical names: 'Build Validation', 'Link Issues', 'Publish Validation', 'Release Notes Preview', 'SBOM Preview'.

errors.title: Error findings
errors.description: Findings of `error` severity — any of these makes `success` false. Empty array when the run was clean; never null. Preserves the order the checks ran in.

warnings.title: Warning findings
warnings.description: Findings of `warning` severity. These do NOT make `success` false unless the run set `strict-warnings`. Empty array when the run was clean; never null.

order.title: Workspace order
order.description: Workspace names in the order they were validated. A JSON object has no guaranteed key order, so this preserves the sequence `workspaces` alone would lose — the same reason the publish phase carries `publish.order`.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.description: Every workspace with a version difference against the target branch, keyed by workspace name — so a consumer looks one up directly rather than scanning an array. Empty object only when nothing had a version difference; a wave of only `github-only` workspaces still populates this, each with empty `builds`.

ValidationPayload.title: Validation payload
ValidationPayload.description: Phase 2 outcome — the build-validation result, the Validation Checks table, every non-pass finding, the build-centric publish preview (per-package, per-build, per-target readiness), and the unified Release Validation Summary check-run URL.

$schema.title: JSON Schema URL
$schema.description: URL of the hosted JSON Schema this output conforms to. Editors and json-schema-aware consumers use this for hover docs and validation.

phase.title: Phase discriminator
phase.description: `validation` identifies this as a Phase 2 output.

success.title: Succeeded
success.description: The one boolean a consumer should gate on. True when the phase completed with nothing failed — including a run that had nothing to do, which is a success because nothing failed. Read `outcome` for what specifically happened.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One human-readable sentence describing the run. Derived from the structured fields beside it and never authored independently, so the prose cannot drift from the data.

dryRun.title: Dry run
dryRun.description: True when the action ran with `dry-run: true`. Phase 3 publishes nothing in dry-run mode; Phases 1 and 2 still observe and report, but mutations (branch updates, PR creation/updating) are suppressed.

failure.title: Failure
failure.description: Why and where validation failed. Null when `success` is true.

ValidationOutput.title: Validation output (Phase 2)
ValidationOutput.description: The structured `result` output emitted when the action runs in the validation phase (Phase 2). Triggered by a push to the release branch; runs build validation, publish dry-runs, release-notes extraction, and emits the unified Release Validation Summary check-run.

releaseNotes.content:
### Minor Changes

- Added the springLaunch API.

PublishOutcome.title: Phase outcome
PublishOutcome.description: `released` — every workspace completed. `nothing-to-release` — no workspace had a version difference against the target branch; the only genuinely empty run, and a SUCCESS, because nothing failed. `partial` — some workspaces completed and at least one did not. `failed` — workspaces were attempted and none completed. `blocked` — the phase aborted before any workspace was attempted; see `failure` for the stage and reason.

PublishFailureStage.title: Failure stage
PublishFailureStage.description: WHEN the phase stopped or degraded, named by the step that failed. `detect` — released packages could not be determined; `build` — the `ci:build` gate failed, so nothing was packed; `sbom` — an SBOM could not be written (non-fatal; the release loses an asset); `publish` — at least one registry upload failed; `tags` — a git tag could not be created; `releases` — a GitHub release could not be created or updated; `linked-issues` — the post-release issue housekeeping failed. `build` and `detect` abort before any workspace is attempted, so every workspace is `blocked`.

reason.title: Failure reason
reason.description: WHAT went wrong, as a single-line summary. For `build` this is the compiler or task diagnostic; the full transcript is in the job log, not here.

blockedWorkspaces.title: Blocked workspaces
blockedWorkspaces.description: Names of workspaces that were never attempted because of this failure — the same set that carry `outcome: blocked`. Empty array when the failure happened after every workspace had been attempted.

PublishFailure.title: Failure
PublishFailure.description: Why the phase did not complete cleanly, and where it stopped. Null on a clean run. This is the only place the abort reason appears — it is not duplicated onto individual workspaces, which report only that they were `blocked`.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.description: Total workspaces released this run. Zero only when the run had nothing to release.

githubOnly.title: GitHub-only workspaces
githubOnly.description: Workspaces of kind `github-only` — tagged and released, publishing to no registry.

githubWithPackages.title: Registry-publishing workspaces
githubWithPackages.description: Workspaces of kind `github-with-packages` — those that resolved at least one publish target.

blocked.title: Blocked workspaces
blocked.description: Workspaces never attempted because the phase aborted. Zero on a clean run.

packagesResolved.title: Packages resolved
packagesResolved.description: Package publications that were *intended* — one per (package, registry) pair resolved before publishing began. Compare with `packagesPublished` to see how much of the intent was realised.

packagesPublished.title: Packages published
packagesPublished.description: Publications whose bytes were newly uploaded this run.

packagesRecovered.title: Packages recovered
packagesRecovered.description: Publications already present at an identical digest, so nothing was re-uploaded.

packagesFailed.title: Packages failed
packagesFailed.description: Publications that were attempted and did not land.

packagesConfirmed.title: Packages confirmed
packagesConfirmed.description: Publications confirmed resolvable on their registry before the run finished.

packagesHeld.title: Packages held
packagesHeld.description: Publications that succeeded but were not yet resolvable at the ceiling. Non-zero means a downstream install may hit `No matching version` for a few minutes; gate follow-on dispatches on this, not on `success`.

PublishTotals.title: Totals
PublishTotals.description: Aggregate counts, so no consumer has to reduce the workspace map to answer a question about scale. Every number here is derivable from `publish.workspaces`; it is duplicated deliberately.

PublishWorkspaceBumpType.title: Bump type
PublishWorkspaceBumpType.description: The semver bump from `baseVersion` to `version`: `major`/`minor`/`patch` when the `major.minor.patch` core advanced (entering pre mode, `3.0.4` → `3.0.5-beta.0`, is a `patch`); `graduation` for a prerelease leaving pre mode for its own stable version (`3.0.5-beta.0` → `3.0.5`); `prerelease` for a step inside pre mode on the same core (`-beta.0` → `-beta.1`); `unknown` when the base version is null, a version does not parse, or the version did not advance. Unlike validation's `bumpType` there is no `new`: the publish phase only detects workspaces whose existing manifest changed.

PublishWorkspaceReleaseType.title: Release type
PublishWorkspaceReleaseType.description: `prerelease` when `version` carries a SemVer prerelease suffix (`1.2.0-beta.0`); `stable` otherwise. Decides which `releases` channels receive the version.

PublishWorkspaceKind.title: Workspace kind
PublishWorkspaceKind.description: What this workspace is *designed* to do, resolved before any publishing is attempted so it stays meaningful on an aborted run. `github-only` — it publishes to no registry; its release is a version bump, a git tag and a GitHub release. This is the steady state for a private tracking workspace and is NOT a degraded `github-with-packages`. `github-with-packages` — it resolved at least one publish target and is expected to put packages on a registry.

PublishWorkspaceOutcome.title: Workspace outcome
PublishWorkspaceOutcome.description: `released` — the workspace was tagged and released and nothing was uploaded because nothing was meant to be: it is `github-only`, or it declares registry targets and every one excludes this version through its `releases` channel (`filtered-by-releases`). `published` — every package landed on its registry. `recovered` — every package was already present at an identical digest, so nothing was re-uploaded. `partial` — some packages landed and at least one failed. `failed` — the workspace was attempted and nothing landed. `blocked` — the workspace was never attempted because the phase aborted first; see the phase-level `failure`.

PublishedPackageOutcome.title: Package outcome
PublishedPackageOutcome.description: `published` — new bytes were uploaded to this registry; `recovered` — the version was already present with an identical tarball digest, so nothing was re-uploaded and the run treated it as done; `failed` — the upload was attempted and did not land (see `error`); `blocked` — the upload was never attempted because the phase aborted first (see the phase-level `failure`).

PublishTargetReleases.title: Release channel
PublishTargetReleases.description: The target's declared `releases` channel: `all` takes every version (the default when undeclared), `stable` only versions without a prerelease suffix, `prerelease` only versions with one.

id.title: Target key
id.description: The `publishConfig.targets` key this publication was declared under (e.g. `npm`, `github`). Null for a package that publishes through the `access`/`private` fallbacks, which declare no keyed targets.

PublishTargetRef.title: Target declaration
PublishTargetRef.description: The `publishConfig.targets` entry a publication was resolved from: its key and its release channel.

PublishAuthMethod.title: Auth method
PublishAuthMethod.description: How the action set npm up to authenticate — what the action DID, not what npm reports. `token` — the Actions OIDC environment was stripped (always, for GitHub Packages and custom registries — trusted publishing exists only on registry.npmjs.org) or the runner never exposed it (no `id-token: write`), so npm could authenticate only with the npmrc token, if any. `trusted-publishing` — the OIDC environment was passed through, so npm was free to attempt its trusted-publishing exchange. npm does not say which path it took, so a `trusted-publishing` upload with a non-null `credential` may have authenticated with that token instead. More methods may be added; treat an unknown value as opaque.

PublishAuthCredential.title: Credential source
PublishAuthCredential.description: Which input supplied the registry token the action wrote to the npmrc: `github-token` (GitHub Packages), `npm-token` (the public npm registry), `custom-registries`, or `registry-env` (the `<HOST>_TOKEN` environment fallback for a custom registry). Null when no token was written.

reason.title: Why the first attempt failed
reason.description: npm's failure for the first attempt, as reported. Prose, not a contract.

PublishAuthFallback.title: Token fallback
PublishAuthFallback.description: The first attempt failed and the action retried once with token auth and provenance off. `from` is how the first attempt was set up — `trusted-publishing` in the designed case (a package with no trusted publisher configured yet).

credential.title: Credential source
credential.description: Where the npmrc token came from. Null when none was written — a tokenless trusted-publishing attempt.

fallback.title: Token fallback
fallback.description: Set when the token retry ran; null when the first attempt's result stands.

PublishAuth.title: Publish authentication
PublishAuth.description: How the upload to this registry was authenticated, as far as the action can know.

PackageAvailabilityStatus.title: Availability status
PackageAvailabilityStatus.description: `confirmed` — the exact `name@version` resolved on the registry within the ceiling. `held` — the publish succeeded but the version was not resolvable when the ceiling elapsed. On npm the ceiling is `registry-confirm-timeout`, and npm holds new versions during publish-time malware scanning, usually for under three minutes and occasionally much longer. GitHub Packages and custom registries have no such hold, so they get a short ceiling (20s, capped by `registry-confirm-timeout`), and there `held` means the version was not installable when checked. A held package IS published; downstream installs may need to retry. `skipped` — no verdict: either the target was not probed, or the registry refused the read; `reason` says which.

PackageAvailabilitySkipReason.title: Skip reason
PackageAvailabilitySkipReason.description: `disabled` — `registry-confirm-timeout` is 0. `dry-run` — the run uploaded nothing to confirm. `not-probed` — the registry has no npm-protocol read to probe (JSR). `no-read-credential` — a GitHub Packages or custom-registry target the action holds no read credential for (`github-token`, or that registry's `custom-registries` entry); it is never read anonymously, because an anonymous read there is refused rather than answered. `read-denied` — the registry answered the confirmation read 401 or 403: the credential cannot read the package, which says nothing about whether it landed. `not-published` — this package did not publish, so there is nothing to confirm. `not-reached` — it published, but the phase stopped before the confirmation step ran.

waitedMs.title: Wait (ms)
waitedMs.description: Milliseconds spent probing this version. 0 when it was not probed; a `read-denied` skip carries the time the refused read took.

reason.title: Skip reason
reason.description: Why the probe was skipped. Null unless `status` is `skipped`.

PackageAvailability.title: Registry availability
PackageAvailability.description: Whether — and how long it took until — the registry actually served this version after the publish call returned.

localDigest.title: Local digest
localDigest.description: Integrity digest of the locally-packed tarball, in npm's `dist.integrity` format (`sha512-<base64>`) — what this run would have uploaded.

remoteDigest.title: Remote digest
remoteDigest.description: Integrity digest the registry already had on file for this version, in npm's `dist.integrity` format. Equal to `localDigest` on a `recovered` outcome; different on a digest-mismatch `failed` outcome.

PublishRecoveryDigests.title: Recovery digest pair
PublishRecoveryDigests.description: The digest comparison behind a recovery decision. Present when the orchestrator probed the registry — on `recovered` and on a digest-mismatch `failed`; null when the publish went straight to upload.

provenanceUrl.title: Provenance attestation URL
provenanceUrl.description: The action's own SLSA provenance over this tarball, stored as a GitHub artifact attestation (`gh attestation verify`). Written once per build directory and shared by every registry that build published to, so it appears on GitHub Packages and custom-registry entries too. Null when no target in the build requested provenance, or the attestation could not be written. Distinct from `npmProvenanceUrl`.

npmProvenanceUrl.title: npm provenance URL
npmProvenanceUrl.description: npm's own provenance for this upload — the Sigstore transparency-log entry npm emits when it publishes to the public npm registry with provenance. Null for every other registry, for a provenance-off publish (including the token fallback, which disables it), and when nothing was uploaded.

sbomUrl.title: SBOM attestation URL
sbomUrl.description: The CycloneDX SBOM attestation over this tarball, stored as a GitHub artifact attestation. Null when none was emitted.

githubAttestationUrl.title: GitHub attestation URL (unused)
githubAttestationUrl.description: Always null. Both GitHub artifact attestations this action writes have their own fields — `provenanceUrl` and `sbomUrl` — so this field never had a distinct value to carry. Kept so existing readers do not break; do not read it.

provenanceRecovered.title: Provenance attestation recovered
provenanceRecovered.description: True when a provenance attestation already existed for this tarball's sha256 and was reused. False when one was written this run. Null when no attestation step ran.

sbomRecovered.title: SBOM attestation recovered
sbomRecovered.description: True when an SBOM attestation already existed for this tarball's sha256 and was reused. False when one was written this run. Null when no SBOM attestation ran.

PublishedPackageAttestations.title: Attestations
PublishedPackageAttestations.description: Supply-chain anchors over this published tarball.

name.title: Published package name
name.description: The package name as published. This is the name on the tarball, which is NOT necessarily the workspace's own name — a workspace may publish under a different name per target.

version.title: Published version
version.description: The semver version published to this registry.

success.title: Succeeded
success.description: True when this version is on this registry as a result of this run — whether newly uploaded (`published`) or confirmed already present at an identical digest (`recovered`). False for `failed` and `blocked`.

target.title: Target declaration
target.description: The `publishConfig.targets` key and release channel this publication was declared with. Null when the workspace's targets could not be resolved (a `dist/prod/targets.json` binding miss or an unknown `releases` value), so no declaration was matched.

distTag.title: Dist-tag
distTag.description: The dist-tag this upload was published under — the target's channel tag (`latest` for a stable version, the first prerelease identifier such as `beta` otherwise). Null when nothing was uploaded (`recovered`, `failed`, `blocked`).

auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: How the action authenticated `npm publish` for this registry. Present whenever an upload was attempted — on a `published` package and on a `failed` one whose upload was refused. Null when no upload was attempted: `recovered`, `blocked`, or a failure before the upload (pack, probe, missing token, digest mismatch).

anyOf.title: Package URL
anyOf.description: Web page for this package version — npmjs.com, jsr.io or the repository's GitHub Packages page. Null for a custom registry: an npm-protocol registry has no standard web page for a version, and guessing one would publish a link that may not exist. The registry endpoint is `registry.url`; the tarball, when confirmed, is `tarballUrl`.

anyOf.title: Tarball URL
anyOf.description: The registry's own download URL for this version's tarball, read back from the registry after publishing. Null when the version was not confirmed on the registry before the run finished (see `availability`), or when the registry is not probed.

available.title: Available
available.description: True when this exact version was confirmed resolvable on its registry before the run finished. Orthogonal to `success`: a package can be `success: true` (the upload landed) and `available: false` (the registry has not started serving it yet, or the probe was skipped). Read `availability.status` for which.

anyOf.title: Error message
anyOf.description: Why the publish failed. Non-null only when `outcome` is `failed`.

recovery.title: Recovery digests
recovery.description: The digest pair behind a `recovered` outcome or a digest-mismatch `failed`. Null otherwise.

anyOf.title: Tarball digest
anyOf.description: Integrity hash of the published tarball as `sha512-<base64>`. Null when nothing was uploaded.

PublishedPackage.title: Published package
PublishedPackage.description: One package published to one registry. A workspace publishing the same version to three registries produces three entries here, and they may not all share a name.

PublishSkippedTargetReason.title: Skip reason
PublishSkippedTargetReason.description: `filtered-by-releases` — the target's `releases` channel excludes this version (a `stable` target at a prerelease, or a `prerelease` target at a stable version), so nothing was packed or uploaded for it. Not a failure. The same literal the snapshot phase's `skipped[].reason` uses.

name.title: Package name
name.description: The package name this target would have published under — the name on the tarball.

PublishSkippedTarget.title: Skipped target
PublishSkippedTarget.description: A declared registry target this workspace deliberately did not publish to at this version.

name.title: Tag name
name.description: The git tag created for this workspace.

sha.title: Tag SHA
sha.description: Commit SHA the tag points at, taken from the tag-creation call itself. Empty string on a dry-run; when the tag could be neither created nor resolved; when no package was associated with the tag, so it was never processed; or when the releases step failed outright before any tag was processed. Never null, so a consumer reading `.tag.sha` always gets a string.

PublishTag.title: Git tag
PublishTag.description: The git tag cut for a workspace's release.

name.title: Asset name
name.description: File name of the release asset.

url.title: Download URL
url.description: Browser download URL for the asset.

PublishReleaseAsset.title: Release asset
PublishReleaseAsset.description: A file attached to the GitHub release — a tarball, an SBOM, or an API report.

id.title: Release ID
id.description: GitHub's numeric release id. 0 in dry-run, where no release is created.

url.title: Release URL
url.description: Web URL of the GitHub release.

prerelease.title: Prerelease
prerelease.description: Whether GitHub marks the release a prerelease. The action creates a release for a version with a prerelease suffix as one; a release recovered from an earlier run reports the flag GitHub has on record.

assets.title: Release assets
assets.description: Files attached to the release. Empty array when none were uploaded — never null.

PublishRelease.title: GitHub release
PublishRelease.description: The GitHub release created for a workspace. The git tag is a SIBLING of this object, not a child: tags and releases are created by separate operations, so a tag can exist while release creation failed. Nesting the tag here would lose it in exactly that case.

version.title: Released version
version.description: The version this workspace was bumped to and released at.

baseVersion.title: Base version
baseVersion.description: The version the release's base commit recorded — the merged release PR's base, or HEAD's first parent. Null when it could not be read.

distTag.title: Release channel dist-tag
distTag.description: The dist-tag this version resolves to: `latest` for a stable version, the first prerelease identifier otherwise (`beta` for `2.0.0-beta.3`), or `next` when that identifier cannot be a dist-tag. Each `packages[].distTag` is what an upload actually used.

path.title: Workspace path
path.description: Repo-relative directory of the workspace, e.g. `packages/foo`. `.` for a single-package repository.

success.title: Succeeded
success.description: True when this workspace's release completed as intended — every package that should have landed did (whether uploaded or recovered), and the tag and GitHub release were created. False for `partial`, `failed` and `blocked`.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One human-readable sentence describing this workspace's release. Derived from the structured fields on this object and never authored independently, so it cannot drift from them.
examples: Tagged and released on GitHub; no registry target.

packages.title: Published packages
packages.description: One entry per (package, registry) publication. Always an empty array — never null — for a `github-only` workspace, and for any workspace whose publishing never ran. A target the release filter excluded is not a publication; it is listed under `skipped`.

skipped.title: Skipped targets
skipped.description: Declared registry targets that deliberately received nothing at this version, with why. Empty — never null — when every declared target took the version, or none was declared.

tag.title: Git tag
tag.description: The git tag cut for this workspace. Null when no tag was created — the phase aborted before tagging, or tag creation itself failed. Deliberately a sibling of `release` rather than nested inside it: tagging and release creation are separate steps, and a tag can land while the release does not.

release.title: GitHub release
release.description: The GitHub release created for this workspace. Null when none was created — either the phase aborted before releases ran (`outcome: blocked`) or release creation itself failed. Null therefore means *not present*, distinct from an empty `packages` array which means *none were meant to exist*.

PublishWorkspace.title: Workspace release
PublishWorkspace.description: Everything that happened to one workspace: what it is, whether it worked, the packages it put on registries, and the GitHub release it produced.

order.title: Publish order
order.description: Workspace names in the dependency-first order they were processed. A JSON object has no guaranteed key order, so this preserves the topological sequence that `workspaces` alone would lose.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.description: Every workspace in this release, keyed by workspace name — so a consumer looks one up directly rather than scanning an array. Populated even on an aborted run, where entries carry `outcome: blocked`.

PublishPayload.title: Publish payload
PublishPayload.description: The per-workspace detail of the publish phase.

$schema.title: JSON Schema URL
$schema.description: URL of the hosted JSON Schema this output conforms to. Editors and json-schema-aware consumers use this for hover docs and validation.

phase.title: Phase discriminator
phase.description: `publish` identifies this as a Phase 3 output.

success.title: Succeeded
success.description: The one boolean a consumer should gate on. True when the phase completed with nothing failed — including a run that had nothing to release, and a run whose every workspace was `github-only`. False when anything failed or the phase aborted. Read `outcome` for what specifically happened.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One human-readable sentence describing the whole run. Derived from `totals` and never authored independently, so it always agrees with the structured counts. A workspace is the unit that is released; a registry target is one upload to one registry. When `totals.packagesHeld` is non-zero the line ends with ` · N registry target(s) held by the registry`.
examples: 2 workspace(s) released · 0 registry target(s) published · 2 GitHub release(s) created
1 workspace(s) released · 2 registry target(s) published · 1 GitHub release(s) created · 1 registry target(s) held by the registry

dryRun.title: Dry run
dryRun.description: True when the action ran with `dry-run: true`. Phase 3 publishes nothing in dry-run mode; Phases 1 and 2 still observe and report, but mutations (branch updates, PR creation/updating) are suppressed.

failure.title: Failure
failure.description: Why and where the phase failed. Null when `success` is true.

PublishOutput.title: Publish output (Phase 3)
PublishOutput.description: The structured `result` output emitted when the action runs in the publish phase (Phase 3). Triggered by the merge of the release PR; publishes each workspace's packages to every configured registry, generates SBOM and provenance attestations, and creates git tags and GitHub releases.

SnapshotOutcome.title: Phase outcome
SnapshotOutcome.description: `published` — at least one version was published and none failed. `rehearsed` — a dry run; the `skipped` entries with reason `dry-run` are what would have been published. `skipped` — versions were computed but every package was skipped (never published, or no registry target); a SUCCESS. `nothing-to-snapshot` — no pending changesets; a SUCCESS. `partial` — some versions published and at least one failed; the published ones ARE on the registry, so pin them exactly. `failed` — publications were attempted and none landed. `blocked` — the run stopped before publishing; see `failure`.

SnapshotFailureStage.title: Failure stage
SnapshotFailureStage.description: `refused` — a guard refused the run (no `snapshot-tag`, or a ref that is not a feature branch). `version` — the snapshot versioning failed (for example, changesets pre mode). `build` — `ci:build` failed, so nothing was packed. `publish` — at least one publication failed; others may have landed.

reason.title: Failure reason
reason.description: WHAT went wrong, as a single-line summary.

SnapshotTotals.title: Totals
SnapshotTotals.description: Aggregate counts over the three lists.

name.title: Package name
name.description: The name on the tarball: the target's published name, which is not necessarily the workspace's.

version.title: Snapshot version
version.description: The exact prerelease version published, e.g. `1.4.0-next-20260927051500`. Pin THIS; the dist-tag moves with every snapshot run.

directory.title: Packed directory
directory.description: Repo-relative directory the tarball was packed from (the target's built output).

tag.title: Dist-tag
tag.description: The dist-tag this version was published under: always the run's snapshot tag, never `latest`.

SnapshotPublishedPackage.title: Published snapshot
SnapshotPublishedPackage.description: One package version published to one registry under the snapshot dist-tag.

SnapshotSkipReason.title: Skip reason
SnapshotSkipReason.description: `never-published` — the registry has never seen this package; a first publish under a non-latest tag would also claim `latest`, so it is left to the real release. `no-publish-target` — the workspace publishes to no registry (a github-only workspace). `dry-run` — the run rehearsed; this version would have been published. `filtered-by-releases` — the target's `releases` channel excludes this snapshot version, so nothing was packed or uploaded for it.

name.title: Package name
name.description: The skipped package or publication name.

version.title: Snapshot version
version.description: The snapshot version the package was bumped to in the job's working tree.

SnapshotSkippedPackage.title: Skipped snapshot
SnapshotSkippedPackage.description: A versioned package that was deliberately not published, with why.

version.title: Snapshot version
version.description: The version that did not land.

SnapshotFailedPackage.title: Failed snapshot
SnapshotFailedPackage.description: A publication that was attempted (or refused by a guard) and did not land. Its presence makes `success` false.

$schema.title: JSON Schema URL
$schema.description: URL of the hosted JSON Schema this output conforms to. Editors and json-schema-aware consumers use this for hover docs and validation.

phase.title: Phase discriminator
phase.description: `snapshot` identifies this as a snapshot-publish output.

success.title: Succeeded
success.description: The one boolean a consumer should gate on. True when the phase completed with nothing failed — including a run that had nothing to do, which is a success because nothing failed. Read `outcome` for what specifically happened.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One human-readable sentence describing the run. Derived from the structured fields beside it and never authored independently, so the prose cannot drift from the data.

dryRun.title: Dry run
dryRun.description: True when the action ran with `dry-run: true`. Phase 3 publishes nothing in dry-run mode; Phases 1 and 2 still observe and report, but mutations (branch updates, PR creation/updating) are suppressed.

failure.title: Failure
failure.description: Why and where the phase failed. Null when `success` is true.

tag.title: Snapshot tag
tag.description: The dist-tag this run published under.

published.title: Published
published.description: Every version this run put on a registry, in dependency-first order. Render a pnpm `overrides:` block from `name` and `version`.

skipped.title: Skipped
skipped.description: Every versioned package this run deliberately did not publish.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Every publication that did not land.

SnapshotOutput.title: Snapshot output
SnapshotOutput.description: The structured `result` output emitted when the action runs with `phase: snapshot` (explicit only, never auto-detected). Versions pending changesets as `<next>-<tag>-<datetime>` prereleases in the job's working tree (never committed), builds, and publishes every already-published package under the snapshot dist-tag. No git tag, GitHub release, release PR, SBOM or GitHub attestation.

ReleaseOutput.title: Silk Release Action output
ReleaseOutput.description: The phase-discriminated release output contract. Use `phase` to discriminate to the right variant: `branch-management`, `validation`, `publish` or `snapshot`. Every variant carries the same shared top-level fields — `$schema`, `phase`, `success`, `outcome`, `summary`, `dryRun`, `failure`, `totals` — plus a phase-specific payload. **`success` and `outcome` are orthogonal, and that is the point.** `success` is the boolean gate a consumer should filter on; `outcome` is the taxonomy saying what specifically happened, drawn from a per-phase enum. Keeping them separate means a filter written against `success` keeps working when a new `outcome` member is added. A run that had nothing to do is a SUCCESS — nothing failed — and says so through its outcome (`nothing-to-release`) rather than through a separate flag. `summary` is one human-readable sentence derived from the structured fields beside it, never authored independently, so it cannot drift from them. `failure` is null unless the phase failed, and names both the stage it stopped at and why. This replaced the v1 contract's four overlapping signals (`status`, `noop`, `succeeded`, `hasFailures`), whose definitions had already drifted from their own documentation.
